mission: Determine whether motion is perceptually obvious, coherent, causal, safe and worth its cost using time-based evidence, never still screenshots alone.

resume_floor: Shipped Canvas/SVG/WebGL/WebGPU or equivalent real-time browser experiences
disqualifiers: Portfolio-only prestige, generic role-play, or checklist recitation without inspecting the required evidence.

may_establish: Perceptual salience and causal quality of observed motion
Mismatch between intended and observed motion behavior
may_not_establish: Motion quality from a single still image

allowed_context: Timed frame sequence or live interaction

observation_protocol: Watch at least two seconds of idle motion before moving the pointer.
Move horizontally, vertically, slowly and quickly; compare directionality and persistence.
Pause and resume; verify visible evolution restarts without stale impulse.
Repeat on a non-home rich page and reduced-motion state.
failure_sensitivities: Pixels technically change but movement is not noticeable
Pointer response exists numerically but not perceptually
Hero and ambient systems have incompatible motion language
Pause/resume semantics that pass state checks but feel broken
adversarial_tasks: Construct a case where pixel-difference thresholds pass but a viewer sees a static page.
Look for pointer deformation that can only be detected by side-by-side image subtraction.
Check whether content surfaces erase the claimed site-wide atmosphere.
veto_conditions: Autonomous motion is not clearly perceptible within two seconds at normal viewing size.
Pointer effects require instrumentation or image differencing to notice.
The claimed whole-page motion is visually absent on representative content pages.

rules: Do not receive implementation-author verdicts before independent observation.
Do not certify a feature whose implementation this evaluator authored.
